headline: A hot CPI put rate-hike odds back on the table and the AI complex finally cracked: the front end sold, the long end bid, and leadership — not the index — did the bleeding.
summary: The sell-off changed location today. The S&P only lost 1.1% to 7718.9, but the Nasdaq 100 fell 2.0%, SOXX 4.5% (-10.9% on the week), SMH 4.0% (-9.6%), AMD 5.7%, MU 4.1% (-16.0% on the week), ASML 3.9%, TSM 3.4%, NVDA 3.2%. High beta vs low vol fell 4.5% in a session and 9.8% on the week. The flip side was a textbook defensive bid: XLV +2.5% (97th percentile, relative strength turning up), XLP +2.2%, UNH +4.7%, LLY +3.6%, WMT +3.5% with acceleration z=1.24, COST +2.9%, LMT +3.6%. Crucially the laggards outperformed — RSP/SPY +0.5%, XRT/SPY +1.5%, IYT/SPY +0.7%, KRE/SPY +0.3%. This is a de-rating of the leadership, not a liquidation of the index. The regime score fell to -14 from -6 and the credit composite halved to 21 from 42.

A hot CPI print is the proximate cause and it bent the curve the wrong way. The 2-year rose 3bp to 4.82% (+17bp on the month), the 3-month bill 2bp to 4.28% at the 100th percentile of the past year, while the 10-year fell 2bp to 5.19% and the 30-year 4bp to 5.52% (-15bp on the week). 2s10s compressed 5bp to 37bp, -14bp on the week, with acceleration z=1.02. Hike odds up at the front, growth doubt at the back. The CPI index itself is +36bp on the month with acceleration z=0.61, and yet 5-year breakevens sit at 2.36% and 10-year at 2.35% — the market still refuses to price it as inflation, so it lands on real rates (DFII10 2.84%, +24bp on the month) and on the 30-year mortgage at 7.40%, z=2.06 with acceleration 1.50.

Yesterday's dollar relief lasted exactly one session. DXY is back +0.3% to 102.53 at the 99th percentile, z=1.53 with acceleration z=1.24; EURUSD sits at 1.1169, the 1st percentile of the year, z=-1.79 and accelerating lower. USDMXN added 1.2% to 18.487 — z=3.3, acceleration 2.24, still the single most extreme reading in the book — and USDBRL reversed +1.3%, the first real crack in a month-long carry winner (Brazil's equity compounding is intact: EWZ +12.9% on the month, Bovespa z=1.92 at the 96th percentile). The dollar bid showed up violently in metals: silver -5.6% (-12.1% on the month, 13th percentile), platinum -3.1%, gold -1.2%, GDXJ -5.3%, GDX -4.4%, gold/silver +4.7% in a day. Copper slipped 0.9% but copper/gold is still pinned at the 100th percentile with z=1.48 and acceleration 1.26 — the one series insisting this is growth repricing, not a growth scare.

Hedges are finally twitching but are still cheap relative to the visible stress. VIX +10.5% to 16.87 — only the 19th percentile; VIX3M 18.79 at the 12th; the term structure +5.6% to 0.898 and turning up; SKEW 157.3 at the 87th; MOVE 99 and +18.1% on the month. Credit is the card to watch: HYG -0.4% to 76.81, z=-1.16 at the 28th percentile and rolling over, HYG/IEF -0.6% on the day and -1.1% on the week, LQD at the 14th percentile. The AI-adjacent balance-sheet trades are where the damage concentrated: ORCL -8.8% (-32.1% YTD, 8th percentile), MSTR -5.9%, COIN -4.9%, BTC -2.0%, and the power build-out complex VST -6.5%, CEG -5.5%, GEV -6.2%, ETN -4.5%, with NLR and REMX already at the 0th percentile. Energy is the lone cyclical still bid — WTI +1.0% to 95.06, Brent 105.91, XOM +1.7% and CVX +2.0%, both at the 100th percentile.

good.text: Long duration worked as a hedge: the 10-year fell 2bp to 5.19% and the 30-year 4bp to 5.52%, -9bp and -15bp on the week, with TLT +2.3% and the 10-year real yield -4bp to 2.84%. Bonds are re-establishing negative correlation to equities for the first time in months.

It was rotation, not liquidation: equal-weight beat cap-weight (RSP/SPY +0.5%), retail/S&P +1.5%, transports/S&P +0.7%, regional banks/S&P +0.3%. The index decline was almost entirely a leadership problem.
Health care is a genuine new leadership candidate: XLV +2.5% to the 97th percentile with relative strength turning up (+2.7% 1m, +7.9% 3m), UNH +4.7%, LLY +3.6%, IBB +1.6%.

Energy keeps compounding through the de-rating: XLE +6.7% on the week with relative strength +17.8% over three months, XOM +1.7% and CVX +2.0% both at the 100th percentile, XOP +5.1% on the week, DBC at the 97th percentile.

Copper/gold sits at the 100th percentile, z=1.48 with acceleration 1.26, and is still rising on a day gold and silver were liquidated — the cleanest argument that this is a rate/valuation repricing rather than a demand collapse.
Brazil remains the one EM that works: EWZ +12.9% and Bovespa +11.3% on the month (z=1.92, 96th percentile), relative strength +11.4% versus the S&P.

bad.text: The silicon de-rating broadened from Korea into the whole complex: SOXX -4.5% (-10.9% week), SMH -4.0%, AMD -5.7%, MU -4.1% (-16.0% week), ASML -3.9%, TSM -3.4%, NVDA -3.2%, AVGO -8.0% on the week. KOSPI -5.5% in a session and -13.1% on the week (z=-1.89, acceleration -1.74); EWY -13.0% on the week.

The front end is repricing hike risk off a hot CPI: 2-year 4.82% (+17bp 1m), 3-month bill 4.28% at the 100th percentile, 2s10s -5bp to 37bp and -14bp on the week with acceleration z=1.02. The 30-year mortgage at 7.40% (z=2.06, acceleration 1.50) is the real-economy transmission.
Credit quietly gave up its status as the bull's best card — the composite fell to 21 from 42. HYG -0.4% at z=-1.16 and the 28th percentile, HYG/IEF -1.1% on the week, LQD at the 14th percentile.

The dollar re-accelerated and broke the periphery: DXY 102.53 at the 99th percentile (z=1.53, acceleration 1.24), EURUSD 1.1169 at the 1st percentile, USDMXN +1.2% at z=3.3 with acceleration 2.24, USDBRL +1.3% reversing a month of carry gains.

Precious metals were liquidated, not rotated: silver -5.6% (-12.1% 1m, 13th percentile), platinum -3.1%, GDXJ -5.3%, GDX -4.4%, gold/silver +4.7% in a day and +7.9% on the month. Miners vs metal is accelerating lower at acc z=-1.55.

The AI capex and balance-sheet proxies are breaking fastest: ORCL -8.8% (8th percentile, -32.1% YTD), GEV -6.2%, VST -6.5%, CEG -5.5%, ETN -4.5%, with NLR, REMX and uranium already at the 0th percentile and MSTR -5.9%, COIN -4.9% alongside.

trades.name: Long health care vs short semis
trades.line: Long XLV / short SMH - defensives over silicon
trades.expr: Buy XLV, short SMH dollar-neutral (roughly 1:1 notional). Options version: XLV Dec calls funded by SMH Dec call sales.
trades.thesis: Today the market stopped paying for AI capex and started paying for cash flow. XLV has the strongest relative-strength trend in the sector table (turning up, +2.7% 1m, +7.9% 3m) at the 97th percentile, while semis are unwinding a parabolic move with the entire supply chain breaking together. A rate backdrop where the front end prices hikes punishes long-duration equity and rewards defensives.
trades.trigger: XLV +2.5% today vs SMH -4.0%, SOXX -4.5% and -10.9% on the week; AMD -5.7%, MU -16.0% on the week, ASML -3.9%, TSM -3.4%. High beta/low vol -4.5% in one session. KOSPI -13.1% on the week confirms it is the supply chain, not one name.
trades.stop: SMH/SPY reclaims 0.760 (from 0.734) or SMH trades back above its one-month high; alternatively XLV relative strength rolls from turning_up to down.
trades.target: 8-10% on the pair; XLV relative strength extends toward +8% over 1m while SMH/SPY retraces its +2.9% 1m relative gain.

trades.name: Buy index vol / SPX downside
trades.line: Buy Nov SPY put spreads - vol still cheap vs SKEW
trades.expr: SPY Nov 745/710 put spread, or VIX Nov 20 calls. Size for 1-1.5% of NAV premium.
trades.thesis: Tail pricing and bond vol both say stress, but spot equity vol is still near the bottom of its range. That gap closes when leadership breaks and credit softens at the same time.
trades.trigger: VIX +10.5% to 16.87 but only the 19th percentile; VIX3M at the 12th. Against that: SKEW 157.3 at the 87th percentile (+10.9% on the week), MOVE 99 (+18.1% 1m), and the VIX/VIX3M term structure +5.6% to 0.898 and turning up. Credit composite halved to 21 from 42.
trades.stop: VIX back below 15 with the term structure under 0.85 and SPX making a new high above 7805.

trades.name: Short the AI-power build-out complex
trades.line: Short VST/CEG/GEV basket - capex trade is unwinding
trades.expr: Equal-weight short basket of VST, CEG and GEV; add GRID or NLR as a tail leg. Hedge with a small long in XLU to isolate the capex premium.
trades.thesis: The power/electrification complex was priced on an uninterrupted AI build. With chips de-rating and financing costs re-accelerating at the front end, the terminal-demand assumption is the first thing repriced. These names have the highest beta to that assumption.
trades.trigger: One-session losses of VST -6.5%, CEG -5.5%, GEV -6.2%, ETN -4.5%, GRID -2.7%, NLR -4.9%. NLR is -13.7% on the month at the 0th percentile; uranium -15.8% on the month. ORCL -8.8% is the credit-funded end of the same trade. All three power names still carry positive 1m relative strength, so the unwind is early.
trades.stop: Basket rallies 8% from entry, or SOXX reclaims its one-month high (semis re-rating invalidates the demand doubt).
trades.target: 15-20% decline in the basket; VST toward its 200-day (-1.6% above it now) and through.

trades.name: Short EUR against USD
trades.line: Short EURUSD - dollar re-accelerating at 99th pctile
trades.expr: Short EURUSD spot/futures, or long UUP. High-beta add-on: long USDMXN in small size given the z=3.3 extension.
trades.thesis: Yesterday's dollar pullback was a one-day pressure release, not a turn. A hot CPI that reopens the hike debate while the rest of the G10 is cutting is the cleanest dollar fuel there is, and the dollar is the mechanism that transmits US tightening into EM and commodity liquidations.
trades.trigger: DXY +0.3% to 102.53, z=1.53 with acceleration z=1.24 at the 99th percentile; EURUSD 1.1169 at the 1st percentile with z=-1.79 and acceleration -1.48; USDMXN +1.2% (z=3.3, acc 2.24); USDBRL +1.3% breaking a month-long downtrend; 2-year yield +17bp on the month.
trades.stop: EURUSD back above 1.1330 or DXY below 101.

trades.name: Long energy vs short metals & mining
trades.line: Long XLE / short XME - the only cyclical still bid
trades.expr: Long XLE (or an XOM/CVX pair), short XME, dollar-neutral.
trades.thesis: Energy is the single sector with price, earnings and relative strength all working, and it is the one that benefits from the crude-side bid that is driving the index's real-yield problem. Mining is the opposite: it is long the dollar-sensitive metals that got liquidated today and has no cash-flow story at these rates.
trades.trigger: XLE +6.7% on the week with relative strength +4.0% 1m and +17.8% 3m; XOM +1.7% and CVX +2.0% both at the 100th percentile; Brent 105.91 (+74.1% YTD). Against that XME -3.8% today, -9.3% on the month, relative strength -10.6%, and COPX -4.2% alongside silver -5.6%.
trades.stop: Brent closes below 95, or XLE relative strength flips from up to rolling_over.
trades.target: 10% on the pair over the quarter.

trades.name: 2s10s flattener
trades.line: Pay 2y, receive 10y - curve re-flattening on CPI
trades.expr: Short 2-year Treasury futures (TU) against long 10-year futures (TY), DV01-neutral.
trades.thesis: The consensus steepener assumed cuts. A hot CPI with the front end at 52-week highs and the long end rallying on growth doubt inverts that logic. The curve flattens from both ends in this regime.
trades.trigger: 2s10s -5bp to 37bp, -14bp on the week, acceleration z=1.02, now in the 32nd percentile and rolling over. 3-month bill 4.28% at the 100th percentile, 2-year 4.82% (+17bp 1m), while the 10-year fell 9bp and the 30-year 15bp on the week. CPI index +36bp on the month.

trades.name: Short high yield vs Treasuries
trades.line: Short HYG vs long IEF - credit's best card is slipping
trades.expr: Short HYG against a duration-matched long in IEF; or buy HYG Dec 76 puts outright.
trades.thesis: Credit has been the bull's trump card all autumn. It is now the weakest link in the composite, and high-yield is the vehicle through which an equity leadership de-rating becomes a financing problem for the AI-capex borrowers.
trades.trigger: Credit composite collapsed to 21 from 42 in one session. HYG -0.4% to 76.81 at z=-1.16, the 28th percentile, trend rolling over; HYG/IEF -0.6% on the day and -1.1% on the week (z=-0.78); LQD at the 14th percentile. ORCL -8.8% is the equity tell on exactly this credit.
trades.stop: HYG back above 78.00 or HYG/IEF above 0.865.
